status: Baseline fixtures only; original hostname implementation unchanged.
contract: Call gethostname with length 64 into a zeroed 65-byte array, return raw bytes before NUL or raw errno on failure. Resolver and uname behavior are outside this increment.
fixtures: Compare short native hostname bytes with uname -n and check successful-query errno preservation for zero, EIO and an arbitrary integer. The exact byte comparison requires a stable hostname. macOS applies the existing 63-byte truncation expectation.
local_baseline: Both ordinary fixtures passed in /tmp/martensite-hostname-baseline-final.log and again after adding the boundary fixture in /tmp/martensite-hostname-boundary-final.log. The final-code cargo xtask pr gate exited 0; log: /tmp/martensite-hostname-final-baseline-pr.log. The earlier full gate overlapped fixture edits and is not final-code acceptance.
boundary_probe: The ignored hostname_boundary_in_isolated_namespace fixture was explicitly executed locally twice, inside unshare --user --map-root-user --uts namespaces with only h bytes. Length 63 returned all bytes and preserved errno 12345; length 64 returned ENAMETOOLONG and set that errno. Both executions passed. The host machine hostname was not modified. This is local GNU/Linux x86_64 evidence, not macOS or arm64 boundary coverage.
boundary_invocation: Set MARTENSITE_HOSTNAME_LENGTH to 63 or 64, enter unshare --user --map-root-user --uts, set the child hostname to that many h bytes, then execute the built library test binary with hostname_boundary_in_isolated_namespace --ignored --nocapture. The fixture never changes the hostname itself and is excluded from ordinary test runs.
candidate: Pinned nix gethostname returns full raw bytes in an owned OsString. GNU/Linux must preserve ENAMETOOLONG at length 64; macOS needs its native truncation contract. Larger-buffer errors, raw errno and allocation side effects need verification before implementation.
